title: Which subagent shape a dispatch belongs to
description: A choice over the closed set of mycommand-* agent shapes in agents/. Each option's rubric is lifted from that definition's own declared role. This is the Intent Routing pattern: the decision is made once, at dispatch time, instead of by prose at the receiving end.
actsNote: Nothing acts on an answer from this set. Nothing-acting is the safety mechanism, not shadow mode. See docs/adrs/0008-no-question-set-acts-in-this-campaign.md.
wiredIntoNote: This set is wired into nothing. No dispatch site reads it, and src/hooks/ is untouched by the campaign that added it. See docs/adrs/0010-eval-harness-before-the-layer.md.
closedSetNote: The options are exactly the definitions in agents/. A shape that is not one of them is not a routable answer; adding one means adding a definition and bumping this set's version.

recordedFailure.what: A /god run lost a step when its mycommand-finisher declined to run /review, because that agent's own definition forbids applying edits beyond /clean.
recordedFailure.why: A wrong decision made at dispatch time, by prose. This is the one genuine label this set has, and it is a correction — corrections are rare by construction.

carries: the work the dispatch is for, in one or two sentences
whether the dispatched agent may write code
whether it is expected to stay alive across rounds
state.note: Enough to tell the shapes apart, and no more. Conversation-derived state leaving the device is gated twice, off by default, and printable with --dry-run.

eval.statement: THIS SET CARRIES NO EVAL NUMBERS. Do not look for one elsewhere; none exists. History records which subagent_type a site NAMED, never which was right, so agreement with it would measure reproduction of the status quo including its mistakes — precisely the number that would be read as justifying promotion. The one genuine label is the recorded correction above. A corpus accrues later, from corrections as they occur.

question: Which mycommand-* subagent shape should this dispatch use?

options.label: mycommand-delegate
options.rubric: Runs one whole MyCommand workflow command — /task, /god, /fb or /work — end to end as a delegated unit of work, on its own branch, in its own worktree. Dispatched one per unit by /work, /manage and /improve.

options.label: mycommand-doc-auditor
options.rubric: Audits one document against the code it describes, or evaluates one document for density, and returns an inventory plus proposed edits — never the edited document. Dispatched one per doc, in parallel batches, by /docs and /truncate.

options.label: mycommand-finisher
options.rubric: Finishes a branch that already carries the work — runs /clean and then /pr in one shared context, in a worktree it does not own. Dispatched by /task --sub, and by /god through it.

options.label: mycommand-griller
options.rubric: A read-only adversarial interlocutor that stress-tests one idea, one question per round, and stays alive across rounds so its repo context is paid for once. Spawned once by /dev and continued with SendMessage.

options.label: mycommand-reviewer
options.rubric: Reviews one pull request independently, without inheriting the authoring conversation's framing of it, and returns findings only — it never applies them. Dispatched by /review.

options.label: mycommand-verifier
options.rubric: Runs the repo's own app and reports whether a change is demonstrably true in it — one verdict per round, spawned once and continued with SendMessage. Dispatched by /verify and by /task Step 2.6.
